# *Do you need to request approval of this new supplier?*
## A supplier (in Bolt’s system) is a company that provides something we need, such as a product or a service. It seems this contract would be for the engagement of a new supplier.
## If you want to add a new supplier for Bolt, then from 28 January 2024, you must submit a new supplier approval request via Workday with the required information to the procurement team. Please see details in [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4719673539/Engagement+rules+for+new+suppliers|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/4719673539/Engagement+rules+for+new+suppliers|smart-link] 
## Exception to this requirement are suppliers that will provide Bolt products or services below 10k. In this situation you don’t need to send a new supplier request via Workday. You purchase the product or service on behalf of Bolt and send the invoice to the accounting department. [Check HERE |https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/FIN/pages/4421518987/Purchase+Supplier+invoices]how to submit purchase invoices correctly. This seems to be the case for this contract, since it is estimated to represent an anual spend of 1.100,00 euros.
# *Who needs to approve this contract?*
## According to the [https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/1525121359/Transaction+Approval+and+Signatory+Policy|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/BILP/pages/1525121359/Transaction+Approval+and+Signatory+Policy|smart-link], spend contracts up to 5k annually need commercial terms’ approval by RMs (ie leadership reports).
## Legal approval is not applicable, except if the contract includes specific clauses triggering Legal Approval (e.g. transfer of personal data, exclusivity, penalties). Consequently, no need to initiate legal tickets.

Therefore, it seems this contract only requires commercial approval by RM and no legal review required. Please confirm approval by RM and I will send this contract for signature.

Available Shards
I see two options
Option 1 - rely on the directory_service service and for the logged user, it could present all the services and schemas; at first sight, it should be doable, but as you said, it requires further investigation and validation. The [definition|https://github.com/bolteu/bolt-server/blob/a658d23e2e73d63cfb6a9ec22adf530640c03f89/gen/asyncApi/directory_service/DirectoryInternalAsyncApi.ts#L239] of ServiceInfoResponse interface looks promising. 

Option 2 - your first suggestion, manual input. And, in addition, automatically, we could try to resolve the schema and shard under db-credentials path in secrets portal.  
It worth mentioning the shard is used to compose the full path that hosts the db-credentials in secrets portal.
More precisely, considering taxify_tageting_worker schema and its three shards: delivery, rides and supply, the db coordinates can be found at the below keys in secrets portal

* db-credentials/taxify_tageting_worker/archiver/delivery
* db-credentials/taxify_tageting_worker/archiver/rides
* db-credentials/taxify_tageting_worker/archiver/supply

I have to take back my initial suggestion, RnA integration adds extra protection.

Sorry for back and forth …

Hey Gregor,
We see that indeed the user changed their phone number just before ordering high value business trips. This is the phone number change [check|https://admin-panel.bolt.eu/fraud/calculations/user_sms_confirmation_check/587754102]. In order to change the phone number, a person has to be logged into the account so the fraudster had to have access to the account before. [~accountid:6241865b45ece00069c80128],

If we read clauses 6.3 and 6.3.1 together, they state: “Bolt shall not be liable whether in tort, contract, or otherwise for: any failure of its systems that results in the failure or inability to provide Bolt Services or Bolt Business;”.

This means that Bolt will not be liable regardless of whose fault it is that systems fail.

Now the client’s proposed wording is: “Bolt shall not be liable whether in tort, contract, or otherwise for: any failure of its systems that results in the failure or inability to provide Bolt Services or Bolt Business, *_if the failure is independent of the way Bolt services are provided and is beyond its control_*;“

This means that if, for example, Bolt will not be able to provide the service due to it’s own fault - Bolt will need to compensate the customer. We don’t want that and this is Bolt’s business decision to exclude that liability.

Therefore, accepting the proposed change extends Bolt’s liability and such change may have monetary consequences for Bolt. Therefore, change is not recommended and according to the Contracting Playbook there are no exceptions. If you still consider that such change is necessary, please acquire approval of the Regional Head of Sales.

* adding things on top of the current integration for Telema is not a very feasible option, because the existing integration itself is already very fragile, slow and breaks down every time any minor change is made.

* accountants create accruals to Workday and for that, they check Telema which invoices need to be accrued. This means, the data on Telema should always match with the data on Workday. Auditors also check Telema. As written above, currently such functionality is not possible and it may not be possible at all due to Telema restrictions, because their systems are not made for data input. 

In my opinion, the best solution for this is to step away from Telema (read point number 2 that Witek wrote).

Kyriba cannot decide where a space should be between references, unless a space is added in the input

Workday right now addes a new tag <Ustrd> per invoice, but this causes issues if the number of invoices is more than 4. Anything beyond 4 is lost.

# We are continuously seeking innovative approaches to benefit all parties involved. Price testing is a part of this process, aimed at discovering optimal solutions that positively impact all stakeholders. With this specific test, our goal was to enhance driver utilization and subsequently increase their earnings.
# Since the overall outcome of the test have been positive, with no available data indicating any negative impact on drivers' incomes, there is no basis for claiming compensation. Furthermore, determining the precise impact of the test on individual driver earnings is challenging because income may be influenced by unrelated factors such as weather. Thus, assessing the difference in earnings due to the test is not feasible.

[~accountid:5ad471a8bb811e2b3af9482a] sharing the summary of the approach before I close the ticket:

During Q1 2024, LCM and privacy have aligned on the approach in multiple calls and via Slack. 

*Summary:*

*It should be possible to mention specific brands and promote specific deals available in the Bolt Delivery product/service based on opt-out consent, taking into account the advice by the privacy team provided below.*

*Reasoning:*

Since Bolt Delivery operates as a marketplace, its essence and value lie in offering third-party food and goods for delivery or pickup via its app - making such promotions core to its service. Considering this, the approach should differ from the approach currently taken for offers which do not mention third parties and other brands.

*Lawfulness considerations:*

To ensure the lawfulness of the approach, Eaters LCM team must take into account the following:

* Promotions must align with Bolt Delivery service of selling food and goods from third parties, like menu items or special deals, reflecting the marketplace's primary function.
* Expected by customers are promotions directly relevant to marketplace offerings, such as food deals or new merchant listings, rather than broad, undefined promotions.
* Promotions leading customers away from the Delivery app, or direct offers from merchants that bypass Bolt, would be considered third-party and require opt-in consent.

*Remaining Tasks - Eaters LCM:*

* *Purpose limitation:* tips and discounts with offers from restaurants and stores at the Bolt Delivery platform will require a separate opt-out option to ensure granularity of consents. This will be implemented under a separate “Promotions and Tips” category in the course of re-designing communication preferences settings for Eaters.
* *Real third-party promotions:* Eaters LCM must keep track of real third-party promotions (e.g., VISA collaborations) and continue relying on opt-in consent.
* *Competition law concerns:* fees from partners for sales facilitation must not suggest third-party promotion bias. Such cases must be escalated by Eaters CM to the Product Legal Team to mitigate competition law risks.

*Remaining Tasks - Privacy:*

* *Accountability:* privacy will i) review agreements with merchants/retailers and make sure they detail promotion purposes within Bolt Delivery, avoiding implications of external brand promotions; ii) update Bolt's internal privacy documentation (LIAs, RoPA, etc.) to reflect this.

hey [~accountid:5f1eebc5170ffc0023b27df9],



* When Bolt transfer the eater’s details to the restaurant for preparing and packing the order, the restaurant is treated as an independent data controller. It means the restaurant is then responsible for the lawful use of this data after the order is completed, including printing the receipts and placing it on the order package.
* However, from our side, Bolt also informs them in the contract that they should not use the data for other purposes than packing the order.
* In this case, as the restaurant is an independent data controller and provider of food service, several laws apply to them and require them to keep info about the purchaser of the services and the receipts for their accounting and tax purposes. So we cannot prevent them from retaining this info until it’s required under the law to keep it. It’s allowed by the privacy law.
* Regarding the receipt, it’s also one of the tax rules to issue VAT invoice to the purchaser of the services and the restaurant issues this in this way. However, as we have eater’s concerns, we can rework the way our partners provide these receipts: maybe we can ask them to put it inside or asking why it’s necessary to put it outside the order.

Hey,

Pretty much the criteria is the sum of their payments and how much of their invoices this payment sum pays fully. 

For example, if a company has 10 invoices (each worth of 500€), their debt is basically 5000€. And, if they make one bulk payment of, say, 3200€, only the first 6 invoice will be marked as paid. Because this amount only fully pays the first 6 invoice (3000€). And if they make another payment of 300€ later, then the 7th invoice will be also marked “paid” because the sum they paid so far (3500€) fully covers the first 7 invoice.

Hi [~accountid:712020:0b1ccfcb-3809-460a-88ab-c96985ba329a] , 

1. Yes, the Dotsure account is separate, but AASA pay this. 
2. Neither company sends us data about Dotsure members. Essentially they add new clients and remove clients that did not pay their Dotsure premiums on the Dotsure account each morning. So they do not actually send us anything, but do it themselves. The only time there is data-sharing of client details, is if there is a query that they send us for a specific client/ride. We then load a ticket to review the ride where there is a problem and process refunds, but do not share driver details with them. The only occasions where we share driver details with them is if an item is left in a Bolt, so they can call to retrieve it. If they cannot reach the driver, we load a ticket for CS to contact the driver to return the item. The Bolt Business Portal creates a ride report monthly with usage of the clients, and we share this document with their accounts department at AASA to pay the Dotsure account. 
3. The only other account they have with us it the AASA account, but there is no date sharing. If there is a query on a specific ride, its the same as with Dotsure. They send us the ride/rider detail to locate the ride for refunds etc. We also on occasion share the driver cell if an item is left in the vehicle. Other than these 2 examples, there is no data sharing whatsoever. 

I hope this helps.

If anything is unclear, we can do a quick Huddle when you’re available.

{quote}Thank you for reaching out to us. 2.2 Number of km traveled in the reporting month (according to the data available at the platform level) - no. of km traveled by the respective car when working for the respective operator, i.e. if the car changes 2 or 3 fleets within a month, for example, to be able to provide the number of kilometers for each individual operator - we will provide the number of Km. in the ride

2.3 Active time in the platform in the reporting month - is the time spent in the ride

2.4 Total receipts made by cars through the platform in the reporting month (broken down, total / cash) - the amounts collected from the riders, for the respective operator

2.5 Name and surname (of the driver)

2.6 Identification no (of the driver)

2.7 Status in the reporting month: holder of the authorisation / employee or contractor of the transport operator - any form that is not provided for in GEO 49/2019 is illegal - *even if the courts say otherwise*. The argument was that for legality the content of the declaration must contain the elements provided by law.

*Next steps*:

* this week, the content of the declaration is being submitted to the Ministry of Finance (MoF)
* MoF will notify the *Data Protection Authority* for approval of the content of the declaration (*in the past they had problems with the content of the declarations because they had information that should not have been collected*)
* ANAF will consult with us on the final version of the Order, the structure of the information and the frequency (the reporting period is one month)
* Approval and publication procedure: we requested a transition period of at least 3 months from the moment of publication until the first reporting. They agreed subject to completing the approval steps at the MoF, discussions with CNIF, etc.

||*Name*||*Pros*||*Cons*||
|[Atlas|https://atlasgo.io/getting-started]|* atlas-operator on k8s, we can manage migrations in the same place
* Declarative (state-based) migrations. We just need to define desired end schema and atlas will make alters based on diff between the desired and current schema|* ClickHouse is in Beta
* Since ClickHouse is in Beta, we need to login to Atlas Cloud and allow them to use our telemetry for analytics. Possible in atlas-operator|
|[Goose|https://github.com/pressly/goose]| |* No docker container, we cannot run in k8s|
|[migrate|https://github.com/golang-migrate/migrate]|* Has a docker container, we can run it in initContainer, same as sre-vector-conf
* We can set Github repo as source and run migrations from there|* If migration is failed (e.g. syntax error), you need to fix schema_migrations table manually|
|[Bytebase|https://www.bytebase.com/]| |* Seems too sophisticated for our use-case
* Everything should be configured in UI
* We need to open port to Bytebase
* You are forced to use their UI, migration cannot be started from GitHub|

It can be argued that the registration of players with their name, address and national registration number is a requirement that applies only to licensed games of chance (for example, if the player were to pay a bet). However, taken at face value, the law does not state this specifically and therefore a conservative approach is that this requirement applies to all games of chance. It is therefore a general requirement that must be followed by Bolt for conducting a promotional game. While a breach of this requirement would not count as a serious crime or offence, it may still result in an injunction or prohibition to carry out the relevant activity, and possibly also a fine (the decision to impose a fine and also the fine amount is up to the relevant authority). Therefore, if the Gambling Authority would notice that Bolt has not followed this requirement, they may 1) require Bolt to give explanations on this, 2) order the giveaway to be terminated, and 3) if deemed necessary by their assessment, issue a fine to Bolt.

Please be aware that from trademark law perspective, after the first sale the trademark owner cannot prevent further distribution of its goods. Since, these are original t-shirts it should be ok. 

*We have to stick to the following rules:* 

# In advertising materials and T&C use a disclaimer:  “ This Campaign is not endorsed, controlled, managed or authorized,  sponspored by [Name of the football club].
# Do not use football club logo in any posts. Do not highlight, make bigger, caps lock in the advertising materials the  [Name of the football club]. Do not use hashtags with the name of football club. 
# We can not send push notification with such wording: “Join our Benfica raffle/giveaway”. It creates confusion for the user that we have a partnership with Benfica.

* it is better to avoid using “Benfica” directly in the context of the campaign (e.g. in the Instagram post description). It can be something like this: win *your favourite club* official t-shirt  
* If team wants to mention  [Name of the football club]  in in-app push notifications we definitely need to add the disclaimer also. At least : “Not managed by [Name of the football club] ”. 

# I agree with [~accountid:712020:0641ea87-e832-482b-8673-ab85e9ad6441] that it’s better if user is not chosen by random means but we require some action (e.g. the most creative comment and so on). Randomly choosing winners is always a legal risk from regulatory perspective.

The administrative costs for forwarding the claim to the Enforcement Authority itself are low. It costs *300 SEK* to apply for a payment order. If the Enforcement Authority (Kronofogdemyndigheten) confirms the debt, one can then apply for enforcement by the Enforcement Authority, which costs *600 SEK*. If it emerges during the processing that the claim is disputed, the case can instead be referred to the court, with an additional cost of *2,500 SEK*.

Please note that from the opposing party, only compensation for legal representation costs up to 380 SEK can be demanded. If the case is referred to court, higher legal representation costs may be requested/reimbursed. 

We need to use an external counsel to help with the application to the Enforcement Authority because our internal legal team has no experience from that.

So I discussed the job briefly with the author yesterday and:

* I think we took “design for failure” too literally in this particular case. This [job|https://bolt-lakehouse.cloud.databricks.com/jobs/154260943301941?o=67599377576481] has been constantly failing (timeout) since 25.3 and before it wasn’t any better.
* [Here|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C03EW27BRAL/p1709630115332189] is a thread related to ☝️ 
* The alerting notifications are really annoying and not useful at all - no action is required - yet they draw on-duty attention.
* My take is that this is useful to have such a job, after all, we don’t have to fix the schemas manually, but..
* We should either make it stable and succeeding or turn off the notifications. Personally, I vouch for the first option.
* Maybe the idea is to remove the timeout constraint first and see how long it takes the job to succeed. And then align the schedule to the actual time it takes to finish.
* The [design|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/ENGINEERING/pages/4766629984/Datalake+health+check+service] of the job makes sense IMHO but:
** we need to look at cluster utilisation
** maybe it needs to be audited to see whether there’re points that can be optimised/improved.

_A summarising comment on the new logic:_ 

We have the complication of scheduled orders. They cause two things. First, an order can get updates up to 90 days after {{created_ts}}. And secondly, order tries can be up to 90 days apart from the corresponding orders.
In a small dataset this wouldn't be a problem. We could make sure our fact and data mart tables are always correct by just re-running everything regularly. Or base incremental loading on {{last_ingested_ts}}.
However, we have big data and we work on S3, so loading has to be incremental, everything needs to be partitioned and partitions always have to be limited. To make our incremental load correct, but not impossibly inefficient, we have set up the following logic to process [orders|https://github.com/bolteu/dbt/blob/main/rides/models/core/marketplace/fact_rides_order.sql]:

* in the beginning of the order script set up some incremental loading parameters
* use macros to calculate data intervals to be processed. previously we had logic that simply extended the data interval (data_interval_start-> period_start).
* the new version adds some flexibility. it gives you two new variables: period_start_min_duration and period_start_max_duration. It is up to you to make use of these two dates in your script.
* in case of orders we have 3 different DAGs now:

* 4h dag that processes 8h of data (we've set period_start_min_duration = 8h and period_start_max_duration = 8h)
* 24h dag that processes 48h of all orders (using period_start_min_duration) and 7 days of scheduled orders (using period_start_max_duration)
* weekly dag that processes 7days of all orders (using period_start_min_duration) and 90 days of scheduled orders (using period_start_max_duration)

The same macros are also used in {{fact_rides_order_try}}. However, the way we use the output period_start_min_duration and period_start_max_duration is different.

Hey, [~accountid:5f1a9692b385da00156b98be]! Thank you for your patience. I am ready to provide information regarding your first question “Could you confirm if there are any UK-specific regulations mandating phone support to our users, regardless of the phone number used?“.

*Short answer:* 

{quote}Yes, there are regulations that create an obligation for Bolt to be contactable by phone. There is no distinction between what phone number is used to contact us. As long as user wants to contact us, regardless of their phone number, the obligation exists.{quote}

*Longer answer:*

{quote}There is no express regulation or statute that specifically mandates the provision of customer support via telephone. However, there are a collection of consumer regulations that together create a situation which creates a de facto obligation to be contactable by telephone. It would be risky, and likely a breach of consumer laws, to not provide support via telephone.

Relevant consumer regulations and laws are: Provision of Services Regulations 2009 (“PSRs”), Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations 2008 (“CPUT”), Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013 (“CCRs”) and Consumer Rights Act 2015 (“CRA”).

Please note that CPUT contains a list of banned commercial practices and according to it, it is potentially a breach to those who have contracted us via phone before to now remove our number from website/app. If we want to do it - we need to at least notify users that we are removing the phone number, but this is not recommended anyway since we should be providing a phone number for users to contact us.

Our obligation is to provide a phone number not for full customer support but for general communication, complaints, provision of information and for efficient communication. Which would essentially include customer support.{quote}

Your second question regarding verification questions should be addressed by our Privacy Team. I have requested help from [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] and hopefully we can get input on that too shortly.

I hope this helps. Please let me know if you have any questions.

* If parcel cannot be delivered both to the recipient and to the customer for at least 3 working days, the driver will deliver parcel to a specified in the T&Cs address and the parcel then can be stored there for a period up to 1 year at the customer’s expense.
* Customer’s obligations include:
** ensure proper packaging;
** parcel should not contain certain items like food, animals and valuables;
** to mark on the parcel the delivery address, the name of the addressee and their telephone number.
* The driver/Hopin can charge additional sums in case the delivery address is incorrect and it was more costly to deliver to the actual address.
* If no driver accepts parcel delivery order, with client’s consent, it can be forwarded to Hopin’s contractor and in such case payment can be limited to cash.
* Driver is responsible for damage to the parcel. No limitation to driver’s liability.
* Not possible to withdraw from the contract given that the provision of courier services will begin before the expiry of the withdrawal period from the contract. If order is cancelled after it is accepted by the driver, driver is entitled to payment.

* Turn off the _Battery protect mode_
* Restart the tablet.

* Open the tablet settings
* Choose the _Network and internet_ category
* The Wi-Fi must be enabled and the status must be _Connected_
* The tablet should not be connected to public Wi-Fi. Ask the provider to use their own Wi-Fi or mobile data.
* Android users can reset their Wi-Fi in _Settings - System - Reset options - Reset Wi-Fi, mobile & Bluetooth - Reset settings._
*SIM CARD ISSUES*
* If the provider has our SIM, check if the SIM card is inserted into the tablet. If it isn't a message "no sim - insert sim card" will appear.
* The mobile data need to be enabled. Ask the provider if they have used up their mobile data (they have 10 GB available).

HI

This is the result of the dynamic commission, the calculation of monthly commission does this way that  we are taking less commission from the driver because we are subtracting from the total Fee (App orders) - all bonuses/compensations/ride discounts

To calculate ride discounts ( need to export all orders for the same period and calculated the difference between the client payed and the ride price)

This is due to a new invoicing system we gradually started to adopt in mid-2022 called Dynamic Commission. Drivers' or Fleets' bonuses are now aggregated in their commission and the final sum is displayed only as one row: commission row. For example;

Commission: 100€, Bonuses 25€, Booking Fee 15€, Refunds 10€

Driver will only see a single row in their commission invoice in the amount of 50€ (100-25-15-10).

So, technically [actual commission - bounses/compensations - rider discounts - booking fees = commission on the invoice]

the report show the gross commission (the report shows the commission before all these discounts). on the invoice, the amount is all other things deducted from it (since commission netting is active). So actual commission invoice will never match with report.

Basically:

Commission invoice - the final sum of commission that  shows for the monthly period, how much commission we took from the driver in the end (after refunds, some of their bonuses/compensation, and rider discounts have been deducte- so this is Driver’s expenses this done to decrease Driver’s commission in the end.

But report and app expenses, shows gross amount that that driver owes to us before we deduct refunds/bonuses/compensations/ ride discounts. 

More info about dynamic commission [here|https://taxify.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/COMM/pages/3663265890].

Hi Ruth, thanks for raising the ticket. 

One of our goals is to streamline user verification processes by reducing additional questions and prioritizing communication through verified channels, especially for requests involving any user’s personal data. 

That means when handling any support case, we must always make sure that we are discussing personal information with the account owner; if the email matches and email validation shows the status “ok”, we, by default proceed with the request. 

We can simplify this into two possible scenarios: 



*Scenario 1*: The driver needs to change their email address and has access either to the old email or to the driver portal; *contact from a verified channel*

* Provide the driver with the instructions in the _How to change my account details_ self-help article (The dedicated [article|https://bolt.eu/en/support/articles/115002912973/] for Keyna does not exist yet, but it’s in the Content team backlog right now) [~accountid:613ec5968f2ada00692f09d1] CC, [relevant thread|https://taxify.slack.com/archives/C05DDLBUR0A/p1714373588075559?thread_ts=1713777128.176319&cid=C05DDLBUR0A]
* For cases where the user has access solely to their email, instruct them to request a password reset to that email address and proceed with logging in via email (refer to the screenshot)
* If the user can only access their phone number, guide them to log in using a one-time code (refer to the screenshot)



*Scenario 2*: The driver needs to change their email address but lacks access to both the old email address and the driver portal; *contact from an unverified channel* ([Relevant SD ticket|https://taxify.atlassian.net/servicedesk/customer/portal/47/LSS-33544?token=eyJ0eXAiOiJKV1QiLCJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiJ9.eyJ0Z3QiOiJhbm9ueW1vdXMtbGluayIsInFzaCI6ImVhODQzMDMzN2QwNDljODc4YTI1YWVjZGYyYTYxMGI3NGZhNDBiMTQ1NDIzM2VlMjQ3MmEzNjdiYWUyYjI5ZTgiLCJpc3MiOiJzZXJ2aWNlZGVzay1qd3QtdG9rZW4taXNzdWVyIiwiY29udGV4dCI6eyJ1c2VyIjoiMTQyNjgiLCJpc3N1ZSI6IkxTUy0zMzU0NCJ9LCJleHAiOjE3MTY3OTAzNDMsImlhdCI6MTcxNDM3MTE0M30.-K4LMBx8Mcm6TIJ1lPxzf53ddhuhrfLEB04w0c17Uns] raised with Privacy)

To answer this question: _do we need to request this document from the fleets with the driver's consent_ - the short answer is yes, why:

* To avoid suffering a data breach (i.e. when the fleet owner changes the driver’s personal details without their knowledge/authorization), we need to receive some proof that the FO is authorized to request this data change

The query for tips with order report:

{noformat}select distinct
asc2.name as city,
etl.created_date as invoice_created_date, 
etl.order_id as order_id,
etl."type" as invoice_type,
etl.driver_id as from_agent_id,
etl.from_type as from_agent_type,
etl.from_name as from_agent_name,
etl.from_vat_code as from_agent_vat_code,
etl.from_reg_code as from_agent_reg_code,
etl.to_user_id as to_agent_id,
etl.to_type as to_agent_type,
etl.currency as currency,
etl.sum as invoice_sum,
etl.vat_sum as invoice_vat_sum,
etl.sum_with_vat as invoice_sum_with_vat,
etl.payment_method_type as payment_method_type,
concat('https://invoice.bolt.eu/?s=', cast(etl.uuid as varchar)) as invoice_link,
rh.total_amount as total_amount,
rh.ride_fee_amount as ride_fee_amount,
rh.tips_amount as total_tips
from ng_public.etl_billing_invoicing_rides_user etl
left join ng_public.ride_hailing_invoicing_order_pricing_transaction rh on rh.order_id = etl.order_id and rh.city_id = etl.driver_city_id  
left join ng_public.admin_system_city asc2 on asc2.id = etl.driver_city_id 
where etl.created_date >= DATE('2023-03-01') 
and etl.created_date <= DATE('2023-06-30') 
and etl.from_vat_code like '%32202751%'{noformat}

We should not reissue any invoice upon request for the reasons like no NIP number at the time of issuance and a rider providing the number later, or a rider requesting a change of address or name later on. It is not allowed by the VAT law to reissue invoices for these reasons.

Unless it is our mistake, e.g. the value, subject of the sale, or NIP number is wrongly stated by us, then we reissue the invoice. And we need to report VAT for the new invoice.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

please find below fragment of the interpretation of polish tax authorities (no. 0115-KDIT1-1.4012.613.2019.2.IK, “_Jedna stawka VAT_ dla sprzedaży _pakietu produktów_ o _różnych stawkach VAT”_) according to which it is not allowed to apply 23% VAT for product which originally have lower rate. 

_“From the information presented in the application, it appears that the sale of a set of snacks, consisting of ready-packaged produts made to office workers, is not so closely related to each other as to make their separation artificial. In fact, it is a supply of divisible and independent goods that can be the subject of a separate supply without prejudice to the other benefits. Thus, they do not economically and economically constitute a single, comprehensive whole, despite the fact that they are packaged in a single set selected by the customer._ *_The fact that these goods are delivered to the customer in one set does not make the goods a single product, taxed at a single rate._*

_The recognition of the supply of a set of snacks consisting of separate entrees is also supported by the fact that they are equivalent services,_ *_none of the goods offered as part of the set, be they crisps, a bar or a drink, serves to better the set._* *_None of the products that make up the kit can be attributed a dominant role in the kit, nor do they complement it._* _All the more so since the kit is composed each time at the request of the customer expressed through an application on the website. The delivery of finished products constitutes, as the Applicant pointed out, activities typical of a grocery store, offering various types of products._

_Therefore, it follows from the above that in the present case_ *_we are not dealing with a composite service, but with a set of separate services (deliveries of finished, packaged goods by the manufacturer), subject to VAT under the rules applicable to each service separately._* _Combining these products into one set (without changing the essence and properties of the services constituting it - as indicated in the application - the Applicant does not interfere with the received goods, (…)_ *_does not create a new product and does not prejudge the right to apply a single tax rate_* _(composing a set consisting of, for example, candy bars, crisps and candy does not affect the treatment of the above services under the provisions of the VAT Act as a single complex service)._

*_Thus, sales of snack sets should be taxed at rates appropriate to the goods comprising the set_*_.”_



{color:#ff5630}*Regardless of tax issues applying higher VAT than is required by law might be considered as practice violating collective interests of the consumers.* {color}

From the legal perspective there are no barriers for naming the event “Formula Bolt”

Luckily there are no registered trademarks of this name (i.e., “Formula Bolt”). There are however other trademarks that consist of or contain the word “formula”, but since this event takes inspiration from Formula 1 then this is the most important trademark to consider and avoid. Therefore, please refrain from using in any marketing materials any of the following word marks (as these are all protected trademarks):

* F1
* Formula 1
* Formula One
* FIA Formula One World Championship
* Grand Prix

This includes avoiding any direct references to the event being inspired by Formula 1. In addition, please be sure not to use any of the logos used by Formula 1 (available [here|https://www.formula1.com/en/toolbar/guidelines.html#:~:text=other%20trade%20marks).-,The%20Logos,-You%20may%20not]).

Other than the above, there shouldn’t be any barriers for naming the event Formula Bolt.

h4. TLDR

Current monthly cost is $500/EC2 + $800/Databricks = $1,300. If we used a single cluster of the smallest SQL warehouse the cost would be $750/EC2 + $528/Databricks = $1,278. There is no real cost saving opportunity here.

h4. Details

The EC2 cost of the current setup is ~$500 per month. The Databricks cost is ~$800 per month (~1600 DBUs). The Fivetran cost is a function of rows ingested, so it is unaffected by the destination we use.

The current setup uses an autoscaling cluster with up to 16 slaves, where driver and slaves are all {{i3.xlarge}} on-demand instances, priced at $0.312/hour by AWS and $0.55/DBU (DBU = hour, in this case) by Databricks.

All [SQL warehouse sizes|https://docs.databricks.com/en/compute/sql-warehouse/warehouse-behavior.html#cluster-sizes-for-pro-and-classic-sql-warehouses] use {{i3.2xlarge}} slaves with at least {{i3.2xlarge}} driver, can be spot instances. The smallest SQL warehouse’s EC2 cost is $1.248/hour (with on-demand instances) compared to $0.624/hour of the current setup with a single worker. While SQL classic warehouse is priced at $0.22/DBU, the smallest size uses 4 DBU/hour, compared to 2 DBU/hour of the current setup with a single worker.

When using an SQL warehouse, we can choose a cluster size and min/max number of clusters. The number of slaves in a cluster is fixed by cluster size.

The current all-purpose cluster is stopped 4 hours/day due to inactivity and uses 2.9 DBU/hour when up, so on an average 1 driver and 2 slaves is used. Roughly the same memory and compute power is provided by the smallest SQL warehouse. Assuming it would also be stopped for 4 hour/day due to inactivity, its cost would be 20*30*$1.248=$750 for EC2 (using on-demand) + 20*30*4*$0.22=$528 for Databricks, total $750+$528=$1,278.

:green_circle: Customer signs up for a Business account, accepts the T&Cs and uses the Coupons feature as enabled via the Dashboard and in compliance with the T&Cs.

Also why and how the commission charged to Bolt would work (rather it should be them paying us as the Business Service Fee?)_

🔴 Not ok if Motivizer sells our coupons as vouchers (i.e. collects a fee before the coupon is actually used for a service). _At least not until we’ve confirmed with Commerce Compliance that a particular partner in the relevant market can do so compliantly._

🔴 Not ok for Bolt to sell vouchers. _At least not until validated via the MVRA process for a particular market._

Hey [@josef.kurchishvili|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U04S8HUGQF4] - thanks for raising this sounds interesting. Thoughts below!

*****

*As a recap:*

* The main 'pain point' with DQO is that it could foreseeably be used to evidence that Bolt is making decisions on 'who ought to be allocated work' - we will be asked if any drivers get preferential treatment based on their performance and we'll have to explain the position.

* In around 2 years' time we'll need to set out on our website exactly how DQO works in all EU markets.

*******

*On the new proposal (as mentioned by* [*@josef.kurchishvili*|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U04S8HUGQF4]*):*

* Unless drivers are given an *_active choice_* on whether they want to opt out, then unfortunately the 'pain point' will still exist: Bolt will be making the unilateral choice over who is (and isn't) entitled to a greater access to work. In full 'silent mode' this is marginally less aggravating to the risk profile, yes, but the point of principle is still present.

* .... *_but_* if drivers were given a choice to opt in to, let's say:

{quote}_"_*_Bolt assisted dispatch_*_: we know it can be frustrating to receive rides you don't like... so to try and match you with passengers that suit your preferences, at your choice we can use your data over the past reoccurring [X period / 4 weeks] to allocate rides similar to those you have previously declined (in that period) to other drivers (at first instance)_*_*_*_."_
***That's really hard to explain{quote}

... then as long as there is sufficient transparency over the existence of the feature in app. etc, this would be much better and workable in EU markets (from the reclass side).

* In fact, I think that would be good - giving some choice back to drivers We'd still have to eventually explain 'how it worked' on our website though

* It would be a little less ideal, but subject to privacy team input it may be possible to auto-enrol all drivers into such a 'driver choice' feature - but we'd definitely need lots of comms on the point and make it very easy for drivers to opt out (cc. [@gabriele.kaveckyte|https://taxify.slack.com/team/U05TXQ5NKPW]).

*******

In summary, all versions of DQO without driver choice are subject to the same broad risk profile. There is no such thing as 'prioritising based on choice' because all drivers would be affected'*_But_* all variations of _'deprioritising based on driver choice'_ ought to be workable - privacy input would of course be needed to steer on how opt ins / outs would need to work.

The approach aligns with scenarios where authorities may contact Bolt in imminent life-threatening situations, where information is urgently required by the licensing authority.
# *Clear Definition of "Critical Safety Concern":*
A "Critical Safety Concern" is specifically defined here as a situation involving an imminent threat to human life, necessitating immediate attention to prevent or mitigate serious harm. Examples may include accidents, medical emergencies, or imminent threats to personal safety during a Bolt journey. Additionally, critical information needs to be made available immediately to avoid breaching licensing conditions, as exemplified by Wolverhampton council's requirement for prioritised responses to urgent matters to uphold public safety standards. This highlights the importance of promptly addressing critical safety concerns to comply with regulatory obligations and ensure public safety.
I.e. Condition 2.7 of Wolverhampton (operator conditions)
All requests to provide information by authorised officers shall be prioritised due to their urgency
## _Priority A – These are for matters of a serious nature where there is significant risk to public safety. Within 1 hour of the request being received_
## _Priority B – These are for matters that require further investigation and have potential to be of a serious matter.   Within 4 hours of the request being received_
## Priority C – These are for requests for information pertaining to general complaints.  Within 24 hours of the request being received
## General request, none prioritised. Within 1 week of the request being received.

This would additionally relate to the Knowledge based article  “[+Responding to info requests by authorities or police+|https://beehive.bolt.eu/customer_support/kb/articles/internal/360009243220]” pertaining to a life or death situation.

*Release of data in similar situations to UK authorities (Police)*

# *Consideration of Alternative Solutions:*
An alternative solution could involve adhering to the standard procedure of providing information about a driver or passenger in non-critical situations. This would entail relying on a DPA to release such information in non-serious circumstances. This approach ensures a consistent and secure process, balancing the imperative of public safety with privacy considerations. But relying solely on waiting for a Data Protection Agreement (DPA) in a life-threatening situation could have a negative impact on public perception, collectively posing a heightened threat to the timely and effective protection of human life.
# *Views of the Public Policy Team:*
The idea for this new process came from the Public Policy team to mitigate ambiguity in certain situations. The proactive approach aims to provide clarity and guidance in handling urgent safety cases, aligning with Bolt's practices in its interactions with public authorities in such critical situations.



We acknowledge the clarification provided by the recent Meta ruling regarding the application of the provision related to the necessity to protect vital interests. However, it's important to note that in certain conditions UK law may differ, and in critical situations where there is a risk of loss of life, our protocol necessitates the disclosure of information to prevent such outcomes.

Hi [~accountid:5ed4b18fc3b5390c24a6f905] - I’m sorry for the long delay in getting back to you 🙏 

{color:#4c9aff}+*‘Taking action’ against drivers who are not ‘online / on trip’:*+{color}

As a rule of thumb, Bolt should +*not*+ ‘take formal action’ against drivers (i.e. temporarily block them, issue guidance etc.) if they do something when they are ‘not actively travelling in relation to a ride' - this is because driver obligations concerning safety are only intended to apply when they ‘performing work via our platform’. Drivers do not work for Bolt and they are not under an obligation to work, even when they are online and receiving offers. It would be going outside of our role to treat drivers if they are ‘under our watch: 24/7’.

However, we can make an exception to this if matters are very serious and we have good reason to think that the driver will cause another safety incident. In this case, Bolt could exercise its right to +permanently terminate+ the driver’s ability to access the platform, for safety reasons / to protect Bolt’s reputation. It should be noted that our legal grounds for this are not watertight, so removing the driver from the platform should be considered absolutely essential.

As an alternative, even if incidents occur ‘off-trip’ Bolt will also have the option to terminate a branding agreement help with a driver for any reason (_“we’ve decided to end our branding arrangement with you”_ - timings etc. would be on a case by case basis). If we want branding removed quickly, then it makes sense for Bolt to cover the costs of doing so and to help the driver arrange this. 

Of course, there is practically no easy way of getting the stickers off the car if the driver decides to take offence Bolt terminating the deal and goes rogue…!

{color:#4c9aff}+*Dealing with non-account holders / complaints when drivers are ‘off-trip’*+{color}

Subject to my comments below re: privacy concerns, Bolt can still opt to engage with individuals who report harmful activities to us.

There is not a ‘legal' requirement that safety related complaints *_must_* be made via our app or via the sole account holder. If that does make matters easier for us in the circumstances,  we could ask that people use their Bolt account associated with a trip to help speed things up, but when the person raising the complaint is NOT an account holder, we can still act (if we have enough information to verify the situation). 

One workable approach might be:

* listen to / observe the complaint.
* check that the person is OK and react accordingly.
* offer to take the details of the driver but note that Bolt may not able to take matters further if the driver was not actually using the Bolt platform at the time. 
* if appropriate, refer the person making the complaint to the appropriate local services to take matters further (e.g. the police). 

I’m not sure if the privacy team has anything to add to this: thoughts [~accountid:712020:a7a7d4bc-10ca-44a0-a22e-fa8752330abd] ?

{color:#4c9aff}+*Preventative strategies*+{color}

For obvious reasons, Bolt should not brand vehicles used by drivers that have ‘less than ideal’ safety records - going forward, our branding teams are supposed to be inviting drivers to apply for branding schemes… and we can therefore reject drivers if there are known concerns. However, we ought not advertise externally that branding schemes are only available for drivers with ‘perfect records' as this:

* makes it look like Bolt is managing drivers and limiting earning opportunities as its sees fit (e.g. reclass concerns). 
* would suggest that we allow unsafe drivers on our platform - not a good look!

----

Chargebacks are always initiated through card issuing bank, in most cases as a result of customer complaints of an unknown charge.

Perhaps in better words (from [+*_Adyen_*+|https://www.adyen.com/en_AU/knowledge-hub/understanding-chargebacks]):

*What’s a chargeback?*

A chargeback is a forced refund initiated by a customer’s bank on their behalf. In some cases, a bank will do this unprompted (if it notices fraud or there’s been an error in the process) but usually, it’s initiated by the customer. There are several reasons a customer might want to initiate a chargeback:

* Their card’s been stolen and someone’s using it fraudulently
* They’ve been refused a refund
* They made an accidental purchase or don’t remember making it
* They don’t recognise the trading name used on a billing statement
* They’re trying to get free stuff

----

* Do we have any extra info about these specific chargebacks?
* Do we know exactly why these chargebacks were made?

No. Banks are not obliged to provide merchants with information on chargeback initiation. Chargeback process involves customer providing proof of why they should get their money back to their bank. Should the bank approve, the merchant (Bolt) has a chance to dispute the claim, providing proof why it was a legit tx, eventually potentially resulting in chargeback reversal.

Chargebacks are initiated by the bank. Card (****8659) is issued by Swedbank, they should know. Not sure if we should act as a middleman here, rather PPA can talk to them directly?

Logically a refunded payment cannot be charged back (as money is already returned).

----

Hi, thanks [~accountid:612f31d89976c300693ebaf7] for the summary, and apologies for the delay on my end. Getting back to you with comments/insights from privacy perspective:

* I agree with the proposed steps for dealing with complaints.
* One very important thing will be *_how we communicate it to the driver_*. We need to make sure that it’s clear that we are taking action/reaching out to them following a complaint, and not leave any space for interpretation (drivers are very sensitive regarding tracking their location, their actions on the app, etc.). We need to reassure them that we are reaching out not simply because we ourselves detected any suspicious activity, but because we are taking actions following a complaint. 
* One last point that is important for privacy - *_it should be clear to all parties (Bolt and driver) what the reason for blocking/suspensions/taking other actions is_*. It should be proportionate and the reasons for blocking/other actions should be properly documented. This way, in case the driver escalates the situation to, say, the privacy regulator, we will have a proper trail of actions to defend our position.

{quote}_Have we considered partnering up with any other fuel card companies who might offer a more user friendly service to the drivers? How have other customers of the current partner solved this problem?_{quote}

----

Hey, thanks for your feedback. 

*Business value: it’s an offer we are negotiating for all drivers in France to allow them to benefit from 0.10€/liter of gas in the partner network. current blockers are high deposit for some drivers.* 

*Alternative partnership:* Yes, we're indeed exploring a new partnership with another company, but the key distinction is that we're not purchasing products and services for drivers outright; rather, we're helping to reduce their costs compared to public prices.

Certain products hold significant value for drivers and contribute to their engagement on the Bolt platform. By making these products more accessible through cost reduction, we can effectively retain drivers and foster a stronger sense of belonging within the company.
We have a driver base of +30k drivers, and there is no partnership we can leverage for unlimited free discounts for drivers. At some point, we need to contribute with the partner for a win/win perspective.

This cost reduction strategy operates through two main levers:

1°) We pay for or subsidize a portion of the product/service (via Bolt money) in exchange for a specified number of rides (enhancing engagement on the Bolt platform).

2°) In some cases, additional leverage is needed, leading to direct payments where drivers cover certain costs or fees with their own money to participate in the engagement process. It's risky, I understand but we have no other means to get the drivers accept certain fees or costs)

e.g., *the fuel cards*: We negotiate free discounts for drivers, *fully funded by the partner*. For instance, any Bolt driver can access the discount. However, to monitor transactions and assess the impact of the offer, we require access to data. This is where the card becomes crucial. Card transactions are traceable and easy to manage compared to cash or drivers' payment cards, which necessitate a receipt to activate the discount. Therefore, the card is essential for tracking and monitoring driver transactions and usage information. *However, there are associated costs, such as card fees and deposits, that drivers must cover. Fees and deposits are sometimes a blocker for drivers to take the offer, and we need that Direct Payment to lower that risk.* 


*How other partners are proceeding:* 
1°) the other business partners have a different profile: they are companies or fleet owners who buy the cards, bear the fees and costs, and redistribute them to their drivers (employees).
Bolt drivers are not employees, proceeding this way puts us at risk of reclassification as employee drivers. ([~accountid:62bff85c118b20bee2bdca35] to confirm)

2°) They mentioned a Taxi company [https://www.g7.fr/en/|https://www.g7.fr/en/|smart-link] that proceeded by buying the cards and use direct payments to deduct the card fees on drivers revenue. 



*Last, there is no other more user friendly way to manage such a significant offer without cards*, at least on the French market.

So if the rider requests to reissue the invoice for their own sake in the future, +you can tell them+ +*according to art., 106b ust. 6 VAT law in Poland*++, we are not allowed to do so.+

We partition by created date, so in the unfortunate case where {{company_order.created}} is 23:59:59 and {{company_order_rider_area.created}} is 00:00:00, we might get duplicates should we backfill from source at some point in the future. Hence, I think it would be wise to backfill from source instead of using the queries below. At the last 6 months’ data that hasn’t yet been archived from the source database.

Assuming uniform distribution, the probability of the above issue occurring is 1/3600*24/5% = 1/1,728,000. In April 2024 we had 149,940,718 orders, so it would’ve occurred ~87 times. That’s 1000+ orders per year.

Dear Ahsine Souidi,

 

*Data Subject Access Request – Response* 

 

Thank you for your data subject request, which was received by us on 08 April 2024.

 

After conducting a diligent search for records relating to your access request, we have confirmed that we do process the personal data requested. Data protection law entitles individuals to a copy of their personal data within the search scope – that is personal data, which identifies them, or enables them to be identified from it as a living individual person. 

 

As you may be aware, the right of access under data protection law does not provide an individual with an absolute right of full access to any and all documents containing their personal data. For example, that right should not adversely affect the rights of others, including our trade secrets or intellectual property and in particular the copyright protecting the software.Furthermore, we must point out that if after careful analysis we conclude that our rights or rights of others prevail,  we will not be able to provide you with access to certain documentation where an exemption applies.

 

We will share copies of the personal data we hold about you to which you are entitled. This includes:

* conversation history for trip on 08 April 2024.

 

For information on how we process relevant personal data, we refer you to our Privacy Policy at [Terms and Conditions|https://bolt.eu/en/legal/terms-for-drivers/?category=rides] , which includes further information about:

* The categories of personal data we process;
* The purposes for which we process personal data;
* The recipients or categories of recipients to whom the personal data has been or will be disclosed;
* The criteria we use to determine how long to retain personal data;
* The sources of personal data received from other parties;
* Your rights in relation to your personal data;
* The existence and envisaged consequences of any automated decision-making/profiling of personal data; and
* Details of any transfer of your personal data to third countries or international organisations and the safeguards used for any such transfers.

 

*Your rights* 

 

In addition to your right to access any personal data we hold about you, you have the right to request us to rectify, erase your personal data, restrict the processing of your personal data or to object to such processing. Any such requests that are received will be considered in conjunction with the applicable provisions of relevant data protection laws. 

 

If you are dissatisfied with this response to your request or in relation to any other matter relating to the processing of your personal data, we hope you will continue to work with us to resolve them. You also have the right to complain directly to your data protection/supervisory authority and, depending on the applicable data protection laws in your country, to seek a judicial remedy.

 

If you have any additional questions, please contact our Customer Support Team by replying to this email.

 

 

Yours sincerely,



Bolt,

*Tracking Consents feature - summary (UPD 5.09):*

{panel:bgColor=#deebff}
*Problem*
The ePrivacy Directive (ePD) and DMA require us to ask our users for their consent before we track them with 3rd party services. Not complying with these directives will lower our marketing efficacy and put us at legal risk of being fined.

*Solution*
In order to be compliant we introduced an additional screen where we ask users about their consent:

1] This dialog is displayed: after sign up, after sign in, or after opening the app if the user is already signed in.

2] This dialog is displayed only if the user hasn't configured consents yet. After configuring consents it won’t be displayed anymore.

3] We also added a new section in user preferences in the Rider app: “Privacy -> Tracking services” where users can adjust their consents later.

4] At the moment, the screen will only set up the consents for the specific App (Rides, Food, etc) that a user is accessing. The consent in Rides App will not affect the trackers in Eaters App.

*Rollout:*

* The feature AB test is currently rolled out to *20%* of Riders, Couriers, Eaters and Drivers

*Markets*

* Globally to all markets - to cover the ePrivacy Directive requirements, which applies to operations globally.

*Next steps*

Full rollout waits for the following decisions:

* should "Appsflyer" be moved to "Necessary" category or can it stay as an optional tracker.
{panel}

{panel:bgColor=#eae6ff}
The feature will be revisited in the future, as currently it encompasses the tracking with 3rd party services, which allows compliance with the DMA and may only ensure partial compliance with the ePD.

Privacy and identity team will continue their collaboration to map out how Bolt tracks its users.
{panel}
